open_weight.method: Measured on ROUTED TOKEN TRAFFIC, not on a count of models — one high-volume open model outweighs many rarely-used ones. 'open' = permissive licence (MIT, Apache-2.0) confirmed on the model's HuggingFace repo. 'open-restricted' = weights published under a bespoke licence carrying use restrictions. 'proprietary' = the vendor publishes no weights for that line: Anthropic entirely, Google's Gemini line (Gemma is separate and open), OpenAI apart from gpt-oss. 'unknown' = neither weights nor a stated vendor policy established — it means unestablished, never a guess.

estimated_spend.label: Estimated routed spend (derived)
assumptions: Tokens multiplied by published list prices from /api/v1/models, joined on canonical_slug.
Prompt and completion prices blended 50/50; the true split per model is not exposed.
List rates only - negotiated enterprise pricing is not public and is typically lower.
Price data covers 98.9% of attributed token volume; embedding models without token pricing are excluded.
Covers OpenRouter-routed traffic only, a fraction of each vendor's total volume.
This is NOT enterprise spend. It is an estimate of spend on gateway-routed traffic.

task_segmentation.window_note: This endpoint publishes a trailing 7-day window only — no other window is supported by the API, so this tab cannot follow the global time selector. Every other tab uses the selected window.
task_segmentation.note: Shares are of classified traffic; the unclassified bucket is excluded from the denominator. Data is sampled, so relative shares are published and absolute volumes are not.

known_unknowns.question: Market share across all AI inference
known_unknowns.why: This measures traffic through one gateway. Most enterprise inference goes direct to provider APIs and is invisible here.

known_unknowns.question: Share by industry - healthcare, legal, manufacturing, public sector, academic
known_unknowns.why: A routing gateway observes task type, never caller identity. No usage API exposes industry segmentation. Note: finance and customer support DO appear as task classifications, so those two are measurable - the rest are not.

known_unknowns.question: Enterprise API spend by vendor
known_unknowns.why: No public endpoint exists. The spend figure here is derived from tokens and list prices, covers gateway traffic only, and is not a substitute.

known_unknowns.question: Whether token counts are comparable between vendors
known_unknowns.why: They are not. Each provider's own tokenizer produces the counts, so summing across vendors adds unlike units. Request share is the more comparable measure.

known_unknowns.question: What the excluded stealth models are
known_unknowns.why: 38.1T tokens (4.8% of visible traffic) came from anonymous providers. Vendor, licence and origin are all unknown, so they are excluded from every share rather than attributed.

series.note: Weekly buckets (week starting Sunday, UTC) from rankings-daily. The final partial week is excluded: it covered one day and would render as a false collapse. '_other' is the API's aggregate of models outside the daily top 50; '_unattributed' is stealth and cloaked traffic, excluded from all share denominators.
